use: Shumi wa? is the classic getting-to-know-you question.
notes: Also taste: shumi ga ii (good taste), shumi ja nai (not my thing).

use: Netto de = online, as in netto de katta (bought it online).

example.ja: それ、ネットで調べてみよう。

examplePolite.ja: それ、ネットで調べてみましょう。

notes: Also a net, as in tennis or fishing.

use: X no fan = a fan of X; daifan = a huge fan.

example.romaji: watashi, kono bando no daifan nan da.
example.ja: 私、このバンドの大ファンなんだ。
example.english: I'm a huge fan of this band.

examplePolite.romaji: watashi, kono bando no daifan nan desu.
examplePolite.ja: 私、このバンドの大ファンなんです。
examplePolite.english: I'm a huge fan of this band.

notes: Not an electric fan; that's senpuuki.

use: Chat messages, voicemail or a written note.

example.ja: メッセージ送ったけど、見た？
example.english: I sent you a message, did you see it?

examplePolite.romaji: messeeji o okurimashita ga, mimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: メッセージを送りましたが、見ましたか？
examplePolite.english: I sent you a message. Did you see it?

use: Any scripted TV series, foreign ones too: kankoku dorama (Korean dramas).

example.ja: 今、なんか面白いドラマある？
example.english: Is there any good drama on right now?

examplePolite.romaji: ima, nanika omoshiroi dorama wa arimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 今、何か面白いドラマはありますか？
examplePolite.english: Are there any good dramas on right now?

use: Any show on a channel: news, variety, quiz; scripted series are dorama.

example.romaji: kono bangumi, maishuu miteru n da.
example.ja: この番組、毎週見てるんだ。
example.english: I watch this show every week.

examplePolite.romaji: kono bangumi wa maishuu mite imasu.
examplePolite.ja: この番組は毎週見ています。
examplePolite.english: I watch this show every week.

use: For a creator's films, books, art or anime; sounds a bit formal or fan-like.

example.romaji: kono kantoku no sakuhin, zenbu mita yo.
example.ja: この監督の作品、全部見たよ。
example.english: I've seen all of this director's films.

examplePolite.romaji: kono kantoku no sakuhin wa zenbu mimashita.
examplePolite.ja: この監督の作品は全部見ました。
examplePolite.english: I've seen all of this director's films.
